title: Join a clarinet's upper and lower joints with the bridge-key levers lined up
instruction: Join the upper joint of the clarinet to the lower joint.
context: Done by: instrument repairers, teachers and players (O*NET 49-9063, 25-1121). The upper joint's bridge-key lever must sit over the lower one; turned wrong, the levers clash and bend (a very common school-instrument repair) or miss. The tenon is unkeyed; the angle is read from the levers, and the rule is not stated. Unlike TK-GPLTLT (lugs into slots, as told) and TK-H3MACU (one-way-round jig plate), the turn is continuous and read from two parts.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Lower joint (loose but heavy, 3 kg; body and collar black hard plastic, keys metal), centred 32 cm in front and 7 cm left of the midline: a grey steel stand base 100 x 100 x 6 mm; on it a round black body 50 mm across from 6 to 36 mm up; on that a black socket collar 40 mm square outside with a 32 mm square bore, from 36 to 66 mm up (the rim), so the socket is 30 mm deep. Its bridge-key lever: a blue metal pad 22 mm long (20 to 42 mm out from the joint's axis), 20 mm wide and 15 mm tall, its top 52 mm up (14 mm under the rim). Two silver metal key posts, one each side of the pad: 24 mm long (20 to 44 mm out from the axis), 15 mm wide, 20 to 35 mm either side of the lever's centre line, from 36 mm up to the rim. Upper joint (loose, 0.12 kg): a round black hard-plastic body 50 mm across and 55 mm tall; below its flat shoulder a cork-covered tenon 25 mm across and 25 mm long; its bridge-key lever, blue metal, 20 mm wide: an arm from 22 to 44 mm out from the axis, from the shoulder to 10 mm above it, and a pad from 30 to 44 mm out hanging 12 mm below the shoulder. It stands tenon down, tenon on the table, in a holder: a fixed grey plastic square collar 40 mm outside, 32 mm bore, 15 mm tall, centred 20 cm in front and 20 cm left of the midline. Lot A: the lower joint's lever points straight away from the robot; the upper joint's lever points to the robot's left. Lot B: the lower lever points left; the upper lever points away. Lot C: the lower lever points right; the upper lever points back toward the robot, turned 30 degrees to the right. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial, judged at the end after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the upper joint), with both joints still for 2 s. 1.0 when the upper joint is home and its lever is over the lower joint's lever: its shoulder within 2 mm of the rim's height, its axis within 5 mm of the socket's axis, upright within 5 degrees, and the two levers pointing within 12 degrees of the same direction seen from above. Score 0 otherwise, including a joint standing proud on a key post, a joint home with the levers apart, or a joint still held. Turning the lower joint on its spot is allowed; score 0 for the whole trial if at any point it is moved more than 10 mm or tilted more than 5 degrees. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Lift the upper joint out and stand it tenon down in its holder, its lever pointing as the lot says (A: left; B: away; C: back toward the robot, 30 degrees to the right). Set the lower joint on its spot with its lever pointing as the lot says (A: away; B: left; C: right). Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: A bench mock-up: short joints, square socket collar and bore (the kit builds only upright boxes and cylinders). The loose cork tenon (3.5 mm a side) tests the angle, not a twist-in fit. The rigid levers stop 2 mm apart (real ones are sprung); their blue is a visibility marker. The key posts stand in for the levers clashing; a seated joint can't be twisted past them, it must be lifted. Masses and friction are simulator values. Lots stop a fixed habit, not a memorised replay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
